name: Captopril
executiveSummary: Short-acting ACE inhibitor. Adult HTN: **12.5–50 mg PO every 8–12 h** (usual max **150 mg/day**). Crisis (local practice): **25 mg** PO/SL, repeat at 30–60 min if needed. Pediatrics: **0.3–0.5 mg/kg/dose**. Contraindicated in pregnancy.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypertension and heart failure.
- Diabetic nephropathy / proteinuria (ACEI).
- Hypertensive urgency in ED (PO/SL) when IV is not immediately available — prefer IV agents if emergency with organ damage.

## Precautions

- **Pregnancy (teratogenic)**, prior angioedema, bilateral renal-artery stenosis.
- First-dose hypotension, hyperK, ↑ creatinine — monitor BP, K+, renal function.
- Take 1 h before meals (absorption).

> Interactions: NSAIDs, K+-sparing agents, lithium.

adulto.dose: HTN/HF: start **6.25–12.5 mg**; maintenance **12.5–50 mg every 8–12 h** (usual max **150 mg/day**). Urgency: **25 mg** PO or SL; may repeat **25 mg** at 30–60 min (institutional ceiling).
adulto.administration: PO (relative fasting). SL: chew/dissolve under tongue in crisis per local protocol.
adulto.notes: SL does not replace hypertensive emergency management with organ damage.

pediatrico.dose: **0.3–0.5 mg/kg/dose** every 8–24 h; titration up to **~6 mg/kg/day** in HF/HTN (specialist; weight ceilings).
pediatrico.notes: Start low; watch BP and creatinine.

neonatal.dose: **0.01–0.1 mg/kg/dose** every 8–24 h (very low start) — cardiology/NNU.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypotension, dry cough, hyperK, rash, dysgeusia, angioedema, acute kidney injury in low-flow states.
